extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, students and scholars of modernist literature
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting stylistic and compositional principles exemplified by James Joyce's work (Ulysses, Dubliners, Finnegans Wake) for writers aiming to study or emulate Joyce-era modernist techniques. Focuses on narrative techniques, language experimentation, structure, intertextuality and use of local detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior monologue / stream of consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of interior monologue; stream of consciousness is a hallmark of Joyce's Ulysses and other works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states Ulysses 'paralleled in a variety of literary styles, particularly stream of consciousness' — use interior monologue to present characters' thoughts directly, collapsing boundaries between narration and mind. Example: Leopold Bloom episodes that foreground internal thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meticulous attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Meticulous attention to detail in depiction of setting and quotidian life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce's fictional universe centres on Dublin and its streets and alleyways; the article notes his 'meticulous attention to detail' as an influence on others. Guidance: render specific, concrete local detail (streets, shops, routines) to ground experimental technique and create verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wordplay and linguistic playfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive use of wordplay, puns, and playful manipulation of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'wordplay' among Joyce's stylistic innovations and cites Finnegans Wake's neologisms and playful coinages. Guidance: experiment with etymology, puns, invented words and layered meanings to create density and multiplicity of signification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radical transformation of traditional plot and character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform conventional plot and character arcs; rethink narrative expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce is credited with the 'radical transformation of traditional plot and character development' — e.g., Ulysses reframes episodic action through interiority and stylistic shifts rather than teleological plot. Guidance: prioritize experience, perception, and technique over classical plot structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple literary styles within one work
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a variety of literary styles and registers across episodes or sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ulysses' episodes are 'paralleled in a variety of literary styles' — the novel deliberately shifts voice, form and genre across chapters. Guidance: vary diction, forms (dramatic scripts, catechisms, parodies, pastiches) to achieve tonal and formal contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mythic parallelism and intertextual structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Map contemporary narrative onto classical/mythic structures and other texts (intertextuality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Ulysses parallels episodes of Homer's Odyssey. Guidance: use mythic frameworks (e.g., parallel episodes) and explicit intertextual references to add structural resonance and thematic layering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musicality, counterpoint and formal music influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate musical structures, allusions, and counterpoint into prose composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce's 'meticulous attention to ... music', use of 'thousands of musical allusions', and influence of musical notation and counterpoint (notably in the 'Sirens' episode) are cited. Guidance: consider rhythm, motifs, leitmotifs, contrapuntal layering of voices, and explicit musical allusion when shaping prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental language and neologism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use experimental syntax, dense coinages and invented vocabulary (neologisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finnegans Wake is described as an 'experimental novel' and Joyce is categorized as a 'neologist'. Guidance: push lexical boundaries, create portmanteau words and polyglot blends to evoke meaning beyond conventional vocabulary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of dialects and multilingual elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate dialect words, multilingual vocabulary and regional speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article mentions Triestine dialect words appearing in Finnegans Wake and Joyce's multilingual environment. Guidance: deploy regionalisms, loanwords and code-switching to texture language and situate voice culturally and geographically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of liturgical/parodic forms and parodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ liturgical forms, parodies and pastiche of authoritative registers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce rewrote and drew on Greek Orthodox liturgy and created liturgical parodies in Ulysses. Guidance: parody high registers (religious, legal, academic) to critique or subvert them and to achieve stylistic contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local particularity as route to universality
rubrics_metrics.description: Write about a specific locale in depth so that the particular contains the universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce is quoted: 'I always write about Dublin, because if I can get to the heart of Dublin I can get to the heart of all the cities of the world.' Guidance: develop richly specific setting and characters so that they resonate beyond their locality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing on real life, autobiographical and archival material
rubrics_metrics.description: Base characters, events and detail on personal acquaintances, family and lived experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Joyce's characters often 'closely resemble family members, enemies and friends' and that many novel details were taken from observation. Guidance: mine biography, memory and documentary sources for credible, emotionally resonant material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision, reworking and serial/episodic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Rework earlier drafts and consider serial/episodic modes of composition and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joyce reworked Stephen Hero into A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man and serially published material (The Egoist, The Little Review); Ulysses and parts of Work in Progress were serialized. Guidance: iterative revision and episodic release can shape pacing, reception and formal development.
